governanceNotes: D1 batch 60 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - median-rhomboid-glossitis to squamous-cell-carcinoma (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests solely on the fourteen-case 1979 clinicopathologic series (PMID 485023), which reframes the lesion as chronic hyperplastic oral candidiasis and states that later lesions become permanent and in a few cases may go further to malignant change.

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) evidence class - one small 1979 case series with a qualitative malignant-change statement, no transformation cases enumerated, and no modern cohort confirmation; (ii) historical-natural-history limit - the series predates modern antifungal practice (its own early-lesion antifungal response data suggest treatment alters the historical course) and HPV attribution; (iii) constitutive boundary - the lesion is itself candidal hyperplasia per the anchor series, so no candidiasis edge was authored; (iv) shared-etiology co-occurrence - the denture-stomatitis review's association list is candidal-biofilm co-occurrence, not a secondary pathway; (v) sibling-window discipline - the lichen-planus and erythroplasia-of-queyrat squamous-cell-carcinoma windows keep their own evidence and none is recycled (ME-29).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Median rhomboid glossitis documents rare malignant change at case-series level: the fourteen-case clinicopathologic series reframing the lesion as chronic hyperplastic oral candidiasis states that later lesions become permanent and in a few cases may go further to malignant change, with yeast invasion of the parakeratotic epithelial layers and proliferating acanthosis documented histologically (PMID 485023); the association is recorded as reported malignant-change potential in a small 1979 series only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the located malignant-change statement is a qualitative observation in a fourteen-case 1979 series without incidence denominators, transformation case detail, or modern cohort confirmation, so any individual oral malignancy requires biopsy with leukoplakia, lichen planus, tobacco, and alcohol exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic persistent candidal infection of the midline tongue epithelium drives long-standing hyperplastic inflammation and proliferating acanthosis so malignant transformation results in rare cases, the chronic-inflammation route implied by the series' malignant-change statement and its permanent-lesion observation, but whether this route produced any individual carcinoma remains hypothesized until biopsy and histopathologic records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single small 1979 case-series class only: the malignant-change claim is qualitative with no transformation cases enumerated, the series predates modern antifungal practice and HPV attribution, and no cohort quantifies squamous-cell-carcinoma incidence in median rhomboid glossitis.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No modern cohort quantifies oral cancer incidence in median rhomboid glossitis; the malignant-change statement is a 1979 observation without denominators; the lesion's modern status as candidal hyperplasia with effective antifungal therapy changes the historical natural history; and leukoplakia, lichen planus, tobacco, and alcohol are dominant competing oral-cancer causes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: tobacco- and alcohol-related oral squamous cell carcinoma
oral lichen planus malignant transformation (the published lichen-planus window, not recycled per ME-29)

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at single small case-series class with the historical-evidence limit carried openly: the fourteen-case clinicopathologic series reframing median rhomboid glossitis as chronic hyperplastic candidiasis states that later lesions become permanent and in a few cases may go further to malignant change (PMID 485023); because the malignant-change claim is qualitative in a 1979 series without denominators or modern cohort confirmation and competing oral-cancer causes dominate, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated biopsy with leukoplakia, lichen planus, tobacco, alcohol, and HPV exclusion.
